Title: Unescaped SSR Comment Nodes in Server-Side Rendering (XSS)
Analysis:
During Server-Side Rendering (SSR), Svelte converts template comment nodes (`<!-- comment -->`) directly into HTML comment blocks without escaping. Specifically, in `packages/svelte/src/compiler/phases/3-transform/server/visitors/shared/utils.js` (lines 54–56), the compiler generates SSR code for Comment nodes using the data field directly:
```js
quasi.value.cooked += node.type === 'Comment' ? `<!--\${node.data}-->` : escape_html(node.data);
```
If dynamic values or expression tags are parsed inside a comment node (e.g., when dynamic content or template syntax is nested inside a comment block, or when the `preserveComments` compiler option is active and dynamic comments containing untrusted user inputs are processed), an attacker can supply input containing `-->` to break out of the HTML comment context and inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript tags (e.g., `<script>alert(1)</script>`), leading to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
If a template contains an AST Comment node whose data is supplied by or contains untrusted input:
Input: `--> <script>alert('XSS')</script> <!--`
The output will be rendered as:
`<!----> <script>alert('XSS')</script> <!-- -->`
This terminates the HTML comment immediately and executes the injected script.
